newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS looks to expand in asset management.
newsitem.headline: UBS looks to expand in asset management.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) is stepping up efforts to expand its asset management and private banking businesses, especially in the U.S., and acquisitions are a likely part of this strategy, UBS executives said.

"We must, we want to and we will play a leading role globally in this business," UBS chief executive Mathis Cabiallavetta said at a news conference when discussing the bank group's strategy on asset management.

UBS on Friday reported a 1996 loss of 348 million Swiss francs ($235.7 million) as compared to a 1995 profit of 1.68 billion and said the expected loss was due to previously announced credit risk provisions of 4.4 billion francs.
The bank group also said all three principal contributors to earnings turned in good results. But that it found its asset management in the U.S. was still too weak.
"Our asset management company in New York has not yet found ites definitive position in the U.S. market," Cabiallavetta said.

In detailing the group's strategy for the future now that it has hopefully provisioned sufficiently to address its problemed loan portfolio, Cabiallavetta said acquisitions would probably be a part of this expansion.

"We want to focus our efforts particularly on the expansion of our asset management business both at home and abroad...Obviously, an acquisition is a step that cannot be ruled out entirely," Cabiallavetta said in his remarks.

"This (an acquisition) has been known to be a target for them but other banks are interested in acquisitions too so its quite difficult to find anything at a reasonable price," CS First Boston analyst Madeleine Hofmann said.

"In the past they have always said that they didn't want to pay a lot of goodwill so this confirmation that they are going for an acquisition is for me a slight change in strategy," Bank Julius Baer analyst Hans Kaufmann said.

The UBS executives also said the bank did not intend to expand activities across the board with a view toward becoming a global and traditional investment bank, but would adopt a more selective approach to expansion.

However, perhaps more significant is the fact that UBS said it did not want to become a global investment bank, a statement which further poured cold water on rumours that UBS was interested in some kind of link-up with Merrill Lynch in the U.S.

Swiss Bank Corp has moved in the direction of becoming a powerhouse in investment banking, Credit Suisse wants to play a major role in all areas and UBS is now clearly stating that its ambition to become the "portfolio manager to the world", Kaufmann said.
But in the area of investment banking UBS said it wanted to capitalise on its strength in Europe and Asia.

In the U.S. it wanted to make a limit effort with the aim of becoming a leading player in six industry segments -- Health Sciences, Information Technology, Energy/Natural Resources, Financial Institutions Media/Entertainment and Telecommunications.

Kaufman at Bank Baer also noted that UBS repeated that, as part of its strategy, it wanted to reduce its international loan book, which is not producing good medium-term returns. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340 ($ = 1.476 Swiss Francs)
